newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: S. Korean envoy in Cambodia to head new mission.
newsitem.headline: S. Korean envoy in Cambodia to head new mission.

text.p: Career diplomat Park Kyung Tai arrived in Phnom Penh on Monday to head South Korea's first diplomatic mission to Cambodia since 1975, officials said.

The two countries agreed in May to open low-level diplomatic contacts, deciding against ambassadorial level missions in deference to the wishes of King Norodom Sihanouk, who was close to late North Korean dictator Kim Il Sung.

Hun Sen visited Seoul in July and said he welcomed South Korean aid and investment in Cambodia. The two countries last enjoyed diplomatic ties between 1970 and 1975 when Sihanouk was in enforced exile.

"Our understanding is the king is not going to receive credentials from the South Korean ambassador," said a counsellor at the four-man mission, which effectively opened on August 31 in rooms at the luxury Cambodiana hotel.
He said Park, a career diplomat, was at ambassador level in the South Korean foreign office, but "officially we call him the head of mission." He will head a mini-mission of three other diplomats.
A Cambodian Foreign Ministry spokesman said Park was expected to present his credentials to Foreign Minister Ung Huot at a date to be fixed.
North Korea has maintained an embassy in Phnom Penh since the signing of a landmark peace agreement in 1991.

But the ambassador and three other diplomats were recalled earlier this year after the three junior officers were stopped at the Cambodian-Vietnam border trying to help a former Japanese Red Army activist escape the country.
